findings.evidence: no messages column

findings.summary: Entity matching covers only part of the KYC Screener capability.
findings.evidence: Capability requires entity-file extraction, firm-rule checks, screening and escalation. Source targets are positive/negative matching judgements; no tool-use trajectories or approval decisions. OpenSanctions documents these as same/different logical entities, https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/opensource/pairs/.

findings.summary: Direct entity IDs and referents must stay outside model inputs.
findings.scope: Source metadata and old conversation recipe
findings.evidence: All 10,000 source pairs carry graph IDs and referents; the reproduced baseline includes them in every prompt. 515 positive pairs share the same ID. This is a potential shortcut, not a measured accuracy effect.

findings.summary: 55 observations repeat an unordered entity-ID pair; keep related rows together.
findings.scope: 27 repeated unordered ID-pair groups across all 10,000 records
findings.evidence: Exact ID-pair grouping yields 27 groups / 55 rows. This differs from full-record duplicate definitions. Connected IDs/referents must stay together when partitioning; no held-out split is created by this audit.

findings.summary: 68 negative pairs share a caption; retain them pending label review.
findings.evidence: Counted negative labels where left.caption equals right.caption. These can be legitimate hard negatives; no relabelling or deletion is justified by caption equality.

findings.summary: Identifier-like values remain in entity properties; their effect is unmeasured.
findings.evidence: 2,759 rows have a property value equal to an ID/referent in the source, including wikidataId and relationship fields. These may be legitimate evidence. Removing top-level metadata alone does not prove the absence of shortcuts.
